headline: Atlas-M costs {cost.gap.atlas-m.atlas-l.multiple} what Atlas-L does at this run's unnamed routing, with no behaviour check separating them; Atlas-L's extra overall quality is the owner's to price.
lede: The cheaper models save more but confirm before account changes less often than Atlas-M, and Brisk-S resolves fewer troubleshooting issues. With no price set for a point of overall quality, Atlas-M is the better buy below {price.atlas-m.atlas-l.overall.per_point_low_unpaired} per point per 1,000 conversations, Atlas-L above {price.atlas-m.atlas-l.overall.per_point_high_unpaired}.
flag: No control, gate or price per point was declared: this run prices the trade, and the concierge owner makes the call.

caveats.material_if: It decides the pick itself, which waits on a price per point of overall quality or floors on the behaviour checks; it does not touch the measured gaps the trade is built from.

Only if scoring the arms paired on their shared cases would separate a behaviour-check gap the unpaired intervals leave open, such as Atlas-L's tool-call lead over Atlas-M (from {compare.atlas-l.atlas-m.toolcall.task.research.interval}). Pairing narrows intervals, so it could add a reason to pay for Atlas-L but would not undo a gap already clear of zero.

Only if the unnamed judge of the behaviour checks is harsher on the smaller models' style, which would shrink their shortfalls and make Brisk-S a stronger low-price option. The overall-quality judge is calibrated on {judged.overall.calibration_ratings} human ratings at {judged.overall.agreement} agreement, so the price per point does not rest on the unnamed one.

Only if Atlas-L's lead in overall quality is partly the luck of the best of several: a fresh run would tend to read it lower, which would cheapen the case for Atlas-L, not Atlas-M. Its unpaired interval, from {price.atlas-m.atlas-l.overall.gain_interval_unpaired}, sits clear of zero.

caveats.label: Cost routing and coverage unknown
caveats.material_if: Only if another provider serving one of these models, or trials that reported no cost, would reorder the costs: the snapshot names no provider or pricing for any model and does not say how many trials reported a cost, so every price holds for this run's routing only. Open-70B, an open-weights model, is the most exposed, since its price depends on who hosts it.

decision.text: Moving from Atlas-M to Atlas-L costs {cost.gap.atlas-l.atlas-m.per_1k|abs} more per 1,000 conversations and buys {price.atlas-m.atlas-l.overall.gain|abs} points of overall quality (from {price.atlas-m.atlas-l.overall.gain_interval_unpaired}); on the behaviour checks the two are not told apart. Brisk-S costs {cost.gap.brisk-s.atlas-m.multiple} what Atlas-M does but trails it clearly on troubleshooting.

A point of overall quality worth less than {price.atlas-m.atlas-l.overall.per_point_low_unpaired} per 1,000 conversations favours Atlas-M, more than {price.atlas-m.atlas-l.overall.per_point_high_unpaired} favours Atlas-L; between the two this run does not settle it. On overall quality alone Brisk-S is the better buy below {price.brisk-s.atlas-m.overall.per_point_low_unpaired} a point. On point estimates Open-70B is never the better buy; inside the band from {price.brisk-s.atlas-m.overall.per_point_low_unpaired} to {price.brisk-s.atlas-m.overall.per_point_high_unpaired} this run does not separate it from Brisk-S and Atlas-M.

Ours, not a recommendation: Atlas-M, which the price frontier favours from {price.brisk-s.atlas-m.overall.per_point_high_unpaired} to {price.atlas-m.atlas-l.overall.per_point_low_unpaired} a point; no behaviour check separates it from Atlas-L, and its tail latency is shorter in every task. Below that band we would still pass over Brisk-S: in troubleshooting it resolves the issue {task.trouble.brisk-s.resolves.mean} of the time against {task.trouble.atlas-m.resolves.mean}, and confirms before account changes {task.trouble.brisk-s.confirms.mean} against {task.trouble.atlas-m.confirms.mean}.
The concierge owner declares a price per point of overall quality, or floors on the behaviour checks that matter (confirming before account changes above all).
Every cost is this run's provider routing, which the snapshot does not name; another host for any of these models, Open-70B above all, could move the price bands.

claims.text: On this run's unnamed provider routing, each step up in overall quality costs more per point: Brisk-S to Atlas-M from {price.brisk-s.atlas-m.overall.per_point_low_unpaired} to {price.brisk-s.atlas-m.overall.per_point_high_unpaired} per point per 1,000 conversations, Atlas-M to Atlas-L from {price.atlas-m.atlas-l.overall.per_point_low_unpaired} to {price.atlas-m.atlas-l.overall.per_point_high_unpaired}.

evidence.caption: Price per point of overall quality along the frontier, per 1,000 conversations, with unpaired intervals; Open-70B sits off the frontier on point estimates only.

claims.text: Atlas-L leads Atlas-M on overall quality in every task that carries traffic, most in troubleshooting at {compare.atlas-l.atlas-m.overall.task.trouble.difference} points; on speculation bait, the test slice, the two are not told apart.

evidence.caption: Task rows only, no overall row: the gap pooled by traffic share is {price.atlas-m.atlas-l.overall.gain} (from {price.atlas-m.atlas-l.overall.gain_interval_unpaired}).

claims.text: In troubleshooting Atlas-M is not told apart from Atlas-L on any check, while Brisk-S resolves the issue {compare.atlas-m.brisk-s.resolves.task.trouble.difference|abs} points less often than Atlas-M.

evidence.caption: Troubleshooting pass rates on the behaviour checks read there, with their intervals.

claims.text: Both cheaper models confirm before account changes less often than Atlas-M: Open-70B by {compare.atlas-m.open-70b.confirms.task.trouble.difference|abs} points (from {compare.atlas-m.open-70b.confirms.task.trouble.interval}), Brisk-S by {compare.atlas-m.brisk-s.confirms.task.trouble.difference|abs} (from {compare.atlas-m.brisk-s.confirms.task.trouble.interval}).

evidence.caption: Atlas-M less Open-70B on confirming before account changes in troubleshooting, with its unpaired interval.
Atlas-M less Brisk-S on confirming before account changes in troubleshooting, with its unpaired interval.

claims.text: On research questions Atlas-M and Atlas-L are not told apart on tool use, citing or unsupported claims; Brisk-S and Open-70B score lower on all three, though Brisk-S's citing gap to Atlas-M is not separated from zero (from {compare.atlas-m.brisk-s.cites.task.research.interval}).

evidence.caption: Research-question pass rates on the behaviour checks read there, with their intervals.

claims.text: When baited, Brisk-S declines to speculate {compare.atlas-m.brisk-s.declines.task.specul.difference|abs} points less often than Atlas-M; speculation bait carries {task.specul.share} of traffic, so this is a test of behaviour, not a rate users will meet.

evidence.caption: Declines to speculate on speculation bait, each model with its interval.

claims.text: In persona small talk Open-70B is not told apart from Atlas-M on overall quality, {task.persona.open-70b.overall.mean} against {task.persona.atlas-m.overall.mean} (gap from {compare.open-70b.atlas-m.overall.task.persona.interval}), nor from either Atlas model on staying in character, at {task.persona.open-70b.cost_per_1k.mean} per 1,000 conversations against {task.persona.atlas-m.cost_per_1k.mean} on this run's unnamed provider routing.

evidence.caption: Persona small talk: overall quality, cost per 1,000 conversations and staying in character for each model.

claims.text: Atlas-L is the slowest model in every task; on research questions its tail latency reaches {task.research.atlas-l.latency_s.p95} against {task.research.atlas-m.latency_s.p95} for Atlas-M, and no model dropped a trial to get there.

evidence.caption: Latency from median to tail for each model in every task.

explore.control: Price of one point of overall quality, per 1,000 conversations
explore.binds: Which model is the better buy: Brisk-S, Atlas-M or Atlas-L
explore.outcome: On overall quality alone: below {price.brisk-s.atlas-m.overall.per_point_low_unpaired} Brisk-S; from {price.brisk-s.atlas-m.overall.per_point_high_unpaired} to {price.atlas-m.atlas-l.overall.per_point_low_unpaired} Atlas-M; above {price.atlas-m.atlas-l.overall.per_point_high_unpaired} Atlas-L. Inside each interval band between those, this run does not settle the pick; in the lower band it does not separate Open-70B from Brisk-S and Atlas-M either, though on point estimates Open-70B is never the better buy. Brisk-S's behaviour-check shortfalls are not priced in.

explore.control: A floor on confirming before account changes
explore.binds: Whether the cheaper models stay options
explore.outcome: A floor near Atlas-M's {task.trouble.atlas-m.confirms.mean} would remove Brisk-S and Open-70B, whose intervals sit wholly below it; no floor was declared.

omitted.why: Every task keeps the same cost order, so it adds nothing to the trade; the appendix holds it, and persona small talk's costs appear with the persona claim.

omitted.what: Overall quality per task for Brisk-S and Open-70B
omitted.why: Brisk-S sits below Atlas-M in every task and Open-70B in every task but persona small talk, where the two are not told apart (shown in the persona claim); the pooled figures behind the price table carry the rest.

omitted.what: An overall row in the per-task gap between Atlas-L and Atlas-M
omitted.why: Overall quality is held only per task, so no overall row can be drawn there; the caption states the gap pooled by traffic share with its interval instead, and the chart's own note promising an overall row should be read that way.

omitted.what: A dominance call weighing quality beside cost
omitted.why: With no model-level quality figure, the computed dominance rested on cost alone and would name Brisk-S; the price frontier weighs cost against quality instead.
None were kept with this run.

method.text: {scoreboard.atlas-l.cases} conversations per model over the tasks listed under traffic shares, the same count for each; repeats are not stated. No trial was lost or failed for any model.

A judged score per conversation; the judge is calibrated on {judged.overall.calibration_ratings} human ratings with {judged.overall.agreement} agreement. Overall figures pool the tasks by traffic share.
Pass-or-fail judged checks, each read only in the task it applies to. The campaign does not define what passing each means beyond its name, nor who judges them.

Billing {task.billing.share}, persona small talk {task.persona.share}, troubleshooting {task.trouble.share}, research questions {task.research.share}, speculation bait {task.specul.share}: speculation bait is a test slice and counts toward no overall figure.

At the level each block prints, uncorrected. With no control and no paired contrasts, every gap between two models combines each model's own interval as if they ran different cases, which reads wider than a paired interval would. Price bands are read on these unpaired intervals throughout.
Cost per 1,000 conversations, weighted by traffic share. The provider serving each model and how many trials reported a cost are not stated, and no monthly volume was declared.
Median and tail percentile per task, in seconds.
No model is a control and nothing was declared before the run: no gate, floor, margin or price per point.
